newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends higher but encounters resistance.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends higher but encounters resistance.

text.p: Speculator-linked buying gave a boost to CSCE cocoa futures on Wednesday, dealers said, as the market recorded to its first positive close in four days.
The market sprang higher early in the session, racing through the previous day's high of $1,368. But the run-up was quickly checked by trade and producer selling, dealers said.
Arbitrage selling of New York positions against the London market kept the pressure on late in the day, but prices worked their way back toward the highs by the closing bell.
Front-month March climbed $18 a tonne on the day, to $1,374, having ranged from $1,356 to $1,377. Second-position May gained $17, to $1,397, while the remaining contracts finished $15 to $16 higher.

While the slower pace of Ivorian arrivals compared with last year continues to underpin the market, traders said aggressive selling by Ivory Coast and other producers into the rallies would make significant upside progress difficult.
If it managed to fill a chart gap from $1,375-1,378, March would next take aim at the psychologically important $1,400 level. Major support was seen at $1,350.
The day's volume was estimated at 8,282 lots.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
